title: Community college baseball team involved in tragic accident as 1 dead, 3 airlifted to hospitals - NewsBreak
text:
By Jeremy Goldstein ,
1 hours ago At least one person died while 32 sustained injuries in a bus crash carrying a community college baseball team in rural Iowa on Wednesday, around 110 miles northwest of Des Moines.
The crash occurred at 11 a.m. and only involved the team bus on a highway near Twin Lakes, IA ( Iowa Highway 4). Director of Calhoun County Emergency Services Bruce Musgraves said that three individuals were airlifted to a local hospital.
The bus was carrying 33 people, including the Iowa Lakes baseball team. All riders suffered varying levels of injuries. The identity of the individual killed is still unknown. It came after an ex-NFL star made his feelings clear on Bad Bunny's message just days after a Trump-Obama controversy .

Local police confirmed that the bus veered into a ditch off the side of the northwestern Iowa highway. "The crash remains under investigation," the report from Calhoun County added.
Two injured individuals were taken to Iowa Methodist Medical Center in Des Moines, and 10 others were taken to UnityPoint Health-Trinity Regional Medical Center in Fort Dodge.
The school released a statement about the incident. "Iowa Lakes Community College confirms that members of its baseball team were involved in a bus accident earlier today while traveling," it read.
"Emergency personnel responded immediately to the scene, and injured individuals were transported to area medical facilities for evaluation and care. The College is working closely with local authorities and emergency responders to gather confirmed information," it continued.
"The safety and well-being of our students and staff remain our highest priority. The College is actively supporting those affected and communicating directly with families.
"Out of respect for the privacy of those involved and their families, the College will not be releasing names or additional details at this time. Updates will be provided as more information becomes available and is confirmed by authorities....The College asks for privacy and compassion for all those affected."'
Iowa Lakes was scheduled to face North Arkansas College on Thursday. Their opponents released a statement on Wednesday following the crash.

“Our hearts are heavy as we grieve alongside the Iowa Lakes College community," the North Arkansas College statement read.
"The loss of a life is a tragedy that reaches far beyond one campus.
"We extend our deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of the individual who passed away, and we are lifting up in prayer those who were injured and all who are affected.”
